rv.q: This is a show every bit as magical as the animation, packed with visual thrills and gorgeous choreography alongside signature ballads that gain greater power in their live incarnation.
Michael Grandage's 'Frozen the Musical' production is also fuelled by theatrical magic.
Two hours of Disney Double Plus does the trick.
Its most magical moments will wow every age group.
It's the theatrical equivalent of vanilla ice cream: smooth, sweet and a bit bland.
Samantha Barks as Elsa is both ethereal and commanding in her poise and regality.
The entire evening is filled with nothing but joy and smiles.
Add to that an expanded and updated story and additional music and magic, and Frozen seems to have found its ideal home in the West End, where it deserves to stay for many years to come.
Together the sisters – who now have a song where they reflect their feelings for each other – power the show, bringing warmth to its frozen heart.
Michael Grandage’s handsomely mounted show is still an impressive, twinkling spectacle with a sincere drama at its heart.
The ridiculously incredible cast paired with the best staging you will see in the West End means this show has all the elements for true theatre perfection.
This is one of the few shows that totally swept me away and allowed me to sit back and enjoy the magic.
Frozen is a wonderful, fantastical escape certain to thaw the hearts of even the most cynical.
Diehard fans of the cartoon will be in heaven as everything they know and love is recreated before their eyes.
Every aspect of the show knows where it needs to be and when, making for an enchanting spectacle ready to wow the families who will undoubtedly love it.
While you can never technically fault his slick, entertaining production, it hardly blows you away with its theatrical vision.
The moments that make a young audience gasp make Frozen earn its place on the stage.

cn.t: Disney's Frozen dazzles with spectacular production values, stunning puppetry, and a show-stopping "Let It Go," though some critics find it overly faithful to the film and a bit bland. Strong vocals and old-school theatrical magic win over most audiences.
